triggers.tooltip: Casting |cffffffffOath Breakers|r now triggers |cffffffffZealotry|r on your target and reduces the cooldown of |cffffffffLibrams|r, |cffffffffForce of Golganneth|r, |cffffffffDivine Force|r, and |cffffffffTestament of Will|r by $/1000;505205s1 sec.@s:801450:0@
triggers.reason: the trigger site is confirmed (AscensionTemplarAbilities.cpp:166,185,187, OnSpellCast's Breaker(info) block, calls Zealotry(player, target ? target : player->GetVictim()) on every Breaker cast when 504807 is known; Benediction 801448 matches Breaker() via SpellFamilyFlags[2]=128), but the harness's cast action always sets an explicit unit target (CoAGameplayTest.cpp:7237: targets.SetUnitTarget(target), defaulting to the caster when no target is named), so spell->m_targets.GetUnitTarget() is never null and the player->GetVictim() fallback is unreachable through a trigger_scenario cast. Measured this round: self-casting Benediction 293 times with 504807 known produced 0 casts of 801450 (confirmed via Unit::_IsValidAttackTarget, Unit.cpp:11958-11972: 'can't attack self' returns false for target==player, so Zealotry(player, player) always returns without casting); targeting a hostile dummy directly was also tried and produced 0 Benediction casts at all (Benediction's own EffectImplicitTargetA[0]=21 TARGET_UNIT_TARGET_ALLY rejects a hostile unit target, so the cast itself never completes). There is no trigger_scenario shape that gives the player a live GetVictim() without the harness itself supplying a friendly explicit unit target that overrides it; the harness needs a cast-without-explicit-unit-target action variant before this effect can be built

DBC: Effect[1]=6 (APPLY_AURA), EffectApplyAuraName[1]=42 (PROC_TRIGGER_SPELL), EffectTriggerSpell[1]=801450, ProcFlags=0, ProcChance=100. rev_20260909_04_templar_completion.sql gives 92108 an explicit spell_proc row and registers spell_script_names 92108 -> aura_ascension_templar_event, bypassing the DBC's zeroed ProcFlags; that script's Check (AscensionTemplarEvents.cpp:55-57) fires only on a damaging off-hand auto-attack hit (PROC_FLAG_DONE_MELEE_AUTO_ATTACK, AttackType OFF_ATTACK), unconditional (no roll), then Proc (AscensionTemplarEvents.cpp:120-122) unconditionally casts 801450 (Zealotry()). The effect is reachable and deterministic in principle, but this package's reference Templar carries only a main-hand weapon (classes/templar.json weapon slot 15, no slot 16 entry): grep of src/server/coa/ for SetCanDualWield/CanDualWield shows every call site scoped to CLASS_SON_OF_ARUGAL only (AscensionCompat.cpp:1104-1109, 9583-9594), with no path granting CanDualWield to Templar (ClassId 19); Player::CanEquipItem rejects an off-hand weapon item without CanDualWield (Player.cpp:13412). So the harness's generic equip/attack actions cannot make this class file's reference character land an off-hand swing at all, and no scenario here can observe the proc. Same category of gap as 92109 (a creature-attacker/off-hand-swing driver would be a shared harness capability, better scoped as its own item, not duplicated per-class here).
